Subject: Reliability spotlight: June outage recap + QBR action lanes

Team — attaching a compact postmortem and a CSV of proposed action lanes for QBR prep. High-level summary below; please skim and flag anything you want on the exec slide.

Summary (short):
- Impact: 3 customer-facing regions exposed to increased 5xx rates for ~42 minutes (18:21–19:03 UTC) on June 24. Peak P99 latency spiked to ~2.1s for chat generation.
- Root cause: regression in continuous-batching layer that enabled a pathological kernel fallback path under mixed-length sequences (introduced in runtime v2.14).
- Customer SLA exposure: 6 accounts crossed the 99.9% availability target during the window; Acme Health (priority account) saw degraded throughput for scheduled jobs.

Requested asks for this thread:
1) Confirm owners for each action lane in the CSV (columns: owner, due, impact).
2) Approve suggested customer outreach language (attached).
3) Decide whether to surface a summarized incident note in the QBR deck (I recommend a single slide with timeline, mitigation, and next controls).

I captured timelines and low-level diagnostics in the attached postmortem (compact). Action lanes are intentionally lightweight so we can move fast into QBR and OKR alignment.

Thanks — I want to close the loop on owners by EOD Wednesday so we have slides ready for Friday's QBR dry run.

— Ben

Ben / team — good work on the concise materials. A few OKR-level notes for QBR framing: 

1) Move `runtime hardening` into the Reliability OKR (Q3): target a 3x reduction in P99 regression incidents and an automated canary gating policy. Owner: Vivek (supported by runtime and infra squads).
2) Add a KPI in Product OKRs for `SLO recovery time` — measure MTTR from incident-open to customer-restored baseline (target < 30 minutes by end of Q3).
3) For Acme Health specifically: recommend a targeted QBR slide and a remediation offer (one-time service credit + free Professional Services hours) — please coordinate with Sales (Aditya).

Also: please add one slide showing the proposed operational controls (canary gating, pre-merge perf tests, KV-cache invariants) — that will help the executive conversation stay tactical.

I will slot a 15-minute pre-QBR dry run on Friday at 08:45 PT to review the slide and the customer messaging.
